query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an unmodified α + β dual-phase alloy whose low hardness and poor friction and wear properties limit its use under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could improve its hardness and wear resistance without sacrificing its existing beneficial properties. State the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, applicable operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Plasma nitriding treatment of TC4 (Ti6Al4V) will form a thin, hard TiN-rich surface layer that improves hardness and wear resistance without compromising the alloy’s intrinsic dual-phase benefits.
generation.material_initial_state: Unmodified TC4 (Ti6Al4V) alloy with its inherent α + β dual-phase microstructure, exhibiting relatively low surface hardness and poor friction/wear properties.
generation.intervention: Apply a plasma nitriding treatment at controlled temperatures (e.g., around 800°C) and nitrogen pressures for a defined duration to promote formation of a surface nitride layer.
generation.conditions: Treatment should be performed under conditions that prevent excessive diffusion into the bulk (e.g., short processing time and moderating temperature to avoid alteration of the core microstructure), with wear and friction tests conducted under simulated high-contact-stress operational conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: A TiN-rich surface layer and an underlying diffusion zone containing interstitial nitrogen in the α + β matrix.
generation.mechanism: The introduction of nitrogen forms hard TiN precipitates at the surface and enriches a diffusion zone that impedes dislocation movement. This acts as a barrier to wear and improves the hardness of the TC4 surface without altering the beneficial bulk properties of the alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to untreated TC4, the plasma nitrided alloy will exhibit a significant increase in surface hardness (e.g., an improvement of at least 15-20%) and enhanced wear resistance in high-contact-stress tests, while the core mechanical properties remain largely unchanged.
generation.baseline: Untreated TC4 alloy as currently used, which shows low surface hardness and poor wear performance under extreme service conditions.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies to conditions where the treated surface is subjected to high frictional and contact-stress environments. The plasma nitriding parameters must be tightly controlled (temperature near 800°C, short exposure times) to avoid altering the bulk phase distribution.
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty regarding the optimal nitriding parameters that maximize surface improvements without detrimentally affecting the bulk microstructure. Additionally, long-term performance under cyclic loading and environmental exposure is not fully established.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of TC4 samples, one set undergoing plasma nitriding under the specified controlled conditions and the other remaining untreated as a control. Conduct surface hardness measurements (e.g., microhardness testing), wear tests (e.g., ball-on-disc or pin-on-disc experiments under high-contact-stress conditions), and microstructural analysis (e.g., SEM, XRD) to verify TiN layer formation and diffusion zone characteristics.
measurements: Wear rate via standardized testing (e.g., volume loss or friction coefficient)
Phase and microstructural analysis of the surface layer (e.g., detection of TiN via XRD/EDS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the plasma nitrided samples show less than a 15-20% improvement in surface hardness and do not exhibit a significant reduction in wear rate compared to untreated TC4, or if the treatment adversely alters the core microstructure, then the hypothesis is falsified.
